item.title: Bhikkhus, I say that killing living beings is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that taking…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, I say that killing living beings is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that taking what is not given is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that sexual misconduct is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that false speech is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that divisive speech is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that harsh speech is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that idle chatter is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that covetousness is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that ill-will is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Bhikkhus, I say that wrong view is of three kinds: due to greed, due to hatred, due to delusion. Thus, bhikkhus, greed is a cause for the origination of action, hatred is a cause for the origination of action, delusion is a cause for the origination of action. With the cessation of greed comes the cessation of action, with the cessation of hatred comes the cessation of action, with the cessation of delusion comes the cessation of action.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.174

item.title: A giver of a meal, bhikkhus, a donor, gives five things to the recipient. What five? He gives life, gives beauty, gives happiness, gives strength,…
item.description:
A giver of a meal, bhikkhus, a donor, gives five things to the recipient. What five? He gives life, gives beauty, gives happiness, gives strength, gives eloquence. Giving life, he has a share in life, whether celestial or human. Giving beauty, he has a share in beauty, whether celestial or human. Giving happiness, he has a share in happiness, whether celestial or human. Giving strength, he has a share in strength, whether celestial or human. Giving eloquence, he has a share in eloquence, whether celestial or human. A giver of a meal, bhikkhus, a donor, gives these five things to the recipient.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.37

item.title: Elder Sīlavānīya: A bhikkhu going to the Sītavana forest, Living alone, secluded, content, mind concentrated, Conquering, not terrified, constantly guarding mindfulness of the body.
item.description:
Elder Sīlavānīya:

A bhikkhu going to the Sītavana forest,
Living alone, secluded, content, mind concentrated,
Conquering, not terrified, constantly guarding mindfulness of the body.

From: Theragāthā 1.6

item.title: Elder Nun Guttā: For the supreme goal, Guttā, you went forth, Abandoning even your children, Down to your own self. Practice ardently, Do not let…
item.description:
Elder Nun Guttā:

For the supreme goal,
Guttā, you went forth,
Abandoning even your children,
Down to your own self.
Practice ardently,
Do not let the mind control you.

The mind deceives beings,
Loving Māra's domain.
Through many lives,
They wander, deluded.

Sensual desire and ill-will,
Together with personality view,
Plus clinging to rites and rituals,
And doubt as the fifth.

O bhikkhunī,
Abandon these fetters,
These lower fetters,
You will not return to this life.

Avoid greed and conceit,
Ignorance and restlessness.
Having cut off the fetter of views,
You will end suffering.

Having abandoned the round of birth,
Having fully understood renewed existence,
Not longing for the present,
You will live at peace.

From: Therīgāthā 6.7

item.title: Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Marvelous, Venerable Sir! Venerable Sir, the Blessed One understands the happiness and unhappiness of beings, while humans live in such confusion, such…
item.description:
Wonderful, Venerable Sir! Marvelous, Venerable Sir! Venerable Sir, the Blessed One understands the happiness and unhappiness of beings, while humans live in such confusion, such scum, such deceit. Venerable Sir, humans are confused, while animals are open. Venerable Sir, I can tame an elephant so that whenever it goes to Campā, it displays all its trickery, falseness, wiles, and deceit. But, Venerable Sir, our servants, attendants, and workmen — their bodily conduct is one way, their verbal conduct is another way, their mental conduct is yet another way.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 51 – Kandarakasutta

item.title: Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons, like rain clouds, appear in the world. What four? And how, bhikkhus, is a person with thunder but no…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons, like rain clouds, appear in the world. What four? And how, bhikkhus, is a person with thunder but no rain? Here, bhikkhus, a person speaks but does not act. Thus, bhikkhus, is a person with thunder but no rain. And how, bhikkhus, is a person with rain but no thunder? Here, bhikkhus, a person acts but does not speak. Thus, bhikkhus, is a person with rain but no thunder. And how, bhikkhus, is a person with neither thunder nor rain? Here, bhikkhus, a person neither speaks nor acts. Thus, bhikkhus, is a person with neither thunder nor rain. And how, bhikkhus, is a person with both thunder and rain? Here, bhikkhus, a person speaks and acts. Thus, bhikkhus, is a person with both thunder and rain. Bhikkhus, these four kinds of persons, like rain clouds, appear in the world.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.101

item.title: Sona, when energy is overstrained, it leads to restlessness; when energy is too lax, it leads to laziness. Therefore, Sona, you should establish energy in…
item.description:
Sona, when energy is overstrained, it leads to restlessness; when energy is too lax, it leads to laziness. Therefore, Sona, you should establish energy in balance, penetrate the faculties in balance, and there grasp the sign.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.55

item.title: But this abiding, Ānanda, has been fully realized by the Tathāgata, that is, by not attending to any sign, he attains and abides in internal…
item.description:
But this abiding, Ānanda, has been fully realized by the Tathāgata, that is, by not attending to any sign, he attains and abides in internal voidness. And if, Ānanda, while the Tathāgata is abiding in this abiding, bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, laymen, laywomen, kings, ministers, wanderers, disciples of wanderers come to see him, then, Ānanda, the Tathāgata, with mind inclined towards seclusion, tending towards seclusion, gravitating towards seclusion, living alone, delighting in renunciation, making an end of all states that are based on the taints, speaks only words that are encouraging.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 122 – Mahāsuññatasutta

item.title: - What is good that does not age? What is good that is eternal? What is the treasure of humans? What cannot be taken by…
item.description:
- What is good that does not age?
What is good that is eternal?
What is the treasure of humans?
What cannot be taken by thieves?
- Virtue is good that does not age,
Faith is good that is eternal,
Wisdom is the treasure of humans,
Merit cannot be taken by thieves.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.52

item.title: Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possessing three things has overcome Māra's power and shines like the sun. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possesses the Arahant's aggregate…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possessing three things has overcome Māra's power and shines like the sun. What three? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu possesses the Arahant's aggregate of virtue, the Arahant's aggregate of concentration, and the Arahant's aggregate of wisdom. Possessing these three things, a bhikkhu has overcome Māra's power and shines like the sun.

Virtue, concentration, and wisdom —
For one who has well developed these,
Having overcome Māra's power,
He shines and blazes like the sun.

From: Itivuttaka 59
